summary.title: Disputed trace claim requiring escalation
summary.description: This example represents a case where a trace relationship is claimed by one party but contested or uncertain, requiring structured review and possible escalation to a Dispute Registry.

trace_claim.claim_statement: One party claims that the later work reflects structural influence from an earlier source, while the relationship remains contested or insufficiently resolved.

claimant.statement: The later work appears to reproduce the core structure and conceptual sequence of the earlier source.

responding_position.statement: The later work was independently developed and reflects common discourse rather than direct influence from the claimed origin work.

evidence_items.description: The claimant identifies similarities in the sequence, layered argument structure, and separation between trace, review, and allocation.
observed_features: similar distinction between trace and judgment

evidence_items.description: The later work does not explicitly cite or acknowledge the claimed origin work.
The respondent claims that the later work was developed independently from common background concepts.
observed_features: similar ideas may exist in broader discourse
no direct access evidence is provided in this example

evidence_items.description: The available evidence does not clearly establish whether the later creator accessed or relied on the claimed origin work.
observed_features: no communication record linking the works

evidence.evidence_summary: The case includes moderate structural similarity and lack of citation, but also an independent development claim and insufficient evidence of direct access.

audit_assessment.assessment_summary: The trace claim is plausible enough to document but not strong enough to treat as resolved. The case should be escalated if downstream dispute handling or allocation review is considered.
uncertainty_notes: Structural similarity alone is not sufficient to determine origin.
The absence of citation may be relevant but does not prove intentional omission.
The respondent's independent development claim must be preserved in the audit record.
This example should not be used as a verdict, ownership determination, or allocation basis.

review_notes: Reviewers should preserve both claimant and respondent positions.
Reviewers should not collapse a contested trace claim into a single conclusion.
Additional evidence may be required before any allocation-readiness review.
This case is suitable for Dispute Registry escalation if a formal dispute is opened.

dispute_notes: Origin Audit records the dispute state but does not resolve it.
Formal resolution should occur in a separate Dispute Registry or governance process.

allocation_readiness.reason: The trace claim is disputed and unresolved. Allocation review should not proceed until the dispute status is clarified.
allocation_readiness.recommended_next_step: Escalate to Dispute Registry or conduct additional multi-wing review before considering allocation readiness.

governance_notes.principle: A disputed trace claim must be documented without being prematurely converted into judgment or allocation.
